plain_english_title: Blood Cancers, Anemia, Splenectomy & MGUS: Comparing 1995 and 2018 Rating Rules
what_this_means: Blood and lymphatic disabilities under 38 C.F.R. § 4.117 frequently intersect with Agent Orange (Nehmer), Camp Lejeune, radiation, and PACT Act burn-pit presumptions (including the January 10, 2025 rule at 38 C.F.R. § 3.320b adding acute and chronic leukemias, multiple myelomas, MGUS, myelodysplastic syndromes, and myelofibrosis). Because VA overhauled § 4.117 on December 9, 2018 (83 FR 54250, corrected October 11, 2022 at 87 FR 61248), checking whether a claim was pending or protected before December 9, 2018—and whether secondary organ or nerve complications were rated separately—can substantially change a Veteran's or Survivor's benefits.
record_clues: A retroactive Agent Orange (Nehmer) award for Rai Stage 0 Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (Diagnostic Code 7703) that assigned 0% to claim periods before December 9, 2018, or lowered a pre-2018 running 100% CLL or CML award solely because the rating schedule changed.
An automatic post-treatment rating drop on leukemia, lymphoma, or myeloma without an in-person or clinical VA examination and 60-day advance notice under 38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e).
A 0% rating for Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance (MGUS, Diagnostic Code 7712) where neurology or nephrology records show paraproteinemic peripheral neuropathy or kidney damage.
Combat or trauma spleen removal (Diagnostic Code 7706, 20%) without separate ratings for abdominal-wall muscle injury (Diagnostic Code 5319) or painful surgical scars (Diagnostic Codes 7801 or 7804).
important_cautions: Distinguish Multiple Myeloma from MGUS under Agent Orange Nehmer rules: full symptomatic Multiple Myeloma and AL Amyloidosis (Diagnostic Code 7717) are covered Nehmer conditions under 38 C.F.R. § 3.816, whereas PACT Act § 404 MGUS is a prospective statutory presumption and is excluded from Nehmer class-action back-pay rules.

Sickle cell trait versus sickle cell anemia: under the Note to Diagnostic Code 7714, asymptomatic sickle cell trait alone is not a ratable disability unless accompanied by directly attributable pathological findings, whereas sickle cell anemia is a compensable hereditary blood disease.
Do not rely on the February 17, 2026 medication Interim Final Rule (91 FR 7118)—VA formally rescinded it on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712), so it is not enacted law.

Check exact effective dates (October 23, 1995; March 9, 2012 for Diagnostic Code 7717; December 9, 2018 for the hematologic overhaul; January 10, 2025 for 38 C.F.R. § 3.320b) before alleging error, and remember 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c) allows only one final merits Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) decision per prior Board decision issue.
questions_for_representative: If my CLL or CML rating existed before December 9, 2018—or my Nehmer effective date reaches before December 9, 2018—did VA properly apply the pre-amendment 100% leukemia rule and 38 U.S.C. § 1155 protection?

Since my Multiple Myeloma (Diagnostic Code 7712) carries a 5-year 100% evaluation period, did VA apply both 60-day advance notice (38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)) and 5-year stabilized-rating protections (38 C.F.R. § 3.344) before proposing any reduction?
Do my oncology or neurology records document secondary chemotherapy neuropathy, paraproteinemic nerve damage, kidney impairment, or Housebound / Aid and Attendance Special Monthly Compensation?
If I had a traumatic splenectomy (Diagnostic Code 7706), did VA separately evaluate my abdominal muscle group injury and surgical scar?
